current_example.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+3y(t)-4x(t)+4 \\ {y}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)-2x(t)+{y}^{2}(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of differential equations above. What is the corresponding linearized system at the equilibrium point $\mathbf{x}^\ast=[2, \ 0]^T?$
current_example.worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
\mathbf{x}' = \boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/1afa5c94397af28405a06e0dfb0ab9a57fb264e237d8170526090f8a90041fe7.svg) and 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/ae87d8a2c45873f1bd2b55f31231af19558274d27a491c89a9c8e5f0a0cf445e.svg)

We need to compute the Jacobian matrix (or the total derivative) of $\boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf{x}).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/8516f3df9174ac56cd1f3190407f4e96ae6aa5d84aac78e6608876bb0c6f7daf.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+3y-4x+4)=2x-4,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+3y-4x+4)=3 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-2x+{y}^{2})=2x-2,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-2x+{y}^{2})=2y\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/dff8db2048a87c023e1adac27f2e7b3d215c443aea8f0faf835deff78095cbae.svg)

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/2c4e3326d72e5ad1ccb4a5a60d01764b42203222e4fa26d6566add07b97ea756.svg) to get

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/d78d887dcc64e8365729e106de8da67cc42022f65d402765b2a3d9b38e151a2f.svg)

Finally, near the equilibrium, the nonlinear system is approximated by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/d09ee441d17524f2fa77a93c828971b0a22a30df74dcee459338315b13e61ca3.svg)

where the deviation vector is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14149202/assets/214f2e56c5fcdf8fab4ccd5b654ff4e8ade52a3004e2e3ba065bac739b177da6.svg)
